# Programs both backends build and run

The programs of one file the C and the LLVM backends' tests share, each a feature at a time. Every program here goes through `snello build` and runs as a native binary; the file beside it, `name.out`, is exactly what it prints. `go test ./compiler/emit/llvm/ ./compiler/emit/c/` builds every program here through both backends, as a release and a debug build, and compares its output with the `.out` file; a program without one fails the test. As each slice of a backend lands, the programs it makes buildable are added here.

The programs a reader starts from are under `examples/`; the book's chapters point here for the program each is cut from. To build one:

```
go build -o snello ./cmd/snello
./snello build compiler/emit/internal/backendtest/testdata/fib.snello
./fib
```

The binary is written to the current directory, named after the file.

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| fib.snello | Recursion, integer and float arithmetic, sized integers, conversions |
| strings.snello | `Lines` over text with a carriage return, an empty line, an empty string and a trailing newline; the character classes of a byte; `min` and `max` over integers, floats and a literal; A `ref string` parameter, concatenation, comparison, byte indexing, `Sprintf`, `Printf`, `Sprint` |
| lent.snello | Borrows a call returns, of a string, a slice, a map, a struct, a value with a `Drop`, an option and a `Result`, in every place the compiler could take one for a value made there and release it: on either side of a `+` and in a chain of them, through `??`, an `if` and a `match`, as a statement of its own, passed, compared, converted, ranged over, sliced and printed; after each form the lender holds what it was made with, and a debug build reports a block released early or left at the end |
| control.snello | `if`/`else if`, the three forms of `for`, `continue` and `break`, a loop whose condition and step call functions, a named number type, swap by parallel assignment, `defer` |
| corners.snello | What the lowering to C must get right: literal bases, wrapping overflow, trigraph-looking strings, float printing |
| shapes.snello | Structs and enums: literals, `ref` and `mut` receivers, `match` with bindings, a guard and an or-pattern, a payload changed in place, printing of composite values |
| options.snello | `Map` and `MapErr` on both, with a closure capturing a local, a function value, a function argument that is itself a call, a `Map` inside a `Map`, an owning value moved through, a value with a `Drop` method mapped and passed through, and a mapped error passed up with `?`; `Some`/`None`, `Ok`/`Err`, `?`, `??` with a value, a `panic` and a `return`, `if` with a binding, `if` as an expression, and the order of evaluation when an operand needs statements |
| boxes.snello | `&x` moving a value to the heap, a recursive type through `*Node?`, a pointer lent as what it holds, tuples built, destructured, matched and printed, `()` in a Result |
| slices.snello | An array zero-valued by `var`, indexed to read and write, copied whole, with `len` and `cap`; Slice literals, `make`, checked indexing, sub-slices, every slice method but `Sort`, `range` by index and value and through a `mut`, string methods and their iterators, option and result methods, `==` on composite values, `take` |
| maps.snello | Map literals, `m[k]` reading a missing key as zero and writing a new entry, `+=` on an entry, every map method, `range` in insertion order and through a `mut`, a tuple as a key, growth with removals |
| files.snello | The `os` and `io` packages written in Snello: a temporary directory, `Create`, `WriteString`, `Open`, `ReadToString`, `io.Copy` over the `Reader` and `Writer` traits, `Close`, `RemoveAll`, an `io.Error` printed as its message, `MkdirTemp` under a missing directory reporting the stat of that directory as Go does, `?` on library results, `os.Args`, `os.Stdout` |
| closures.snello | A closure returned from a function with a copy of an `int`, and one that keeps the value of the moment it was made while the variable changes; A closure changing a captured local, function values in a parameter and a field, a named function as a value, a closure inside a closure, `SortBy` and `Sort` |
| generics.snello | One C copy per instance: a generic list with `ref` and `mut` methods and a generic method of its own, `Map` and `Filter` with inferred type arguments, `Empty<f64>()` written, a generic enum matched on, `Pair{a: 1, b: "one"}` inferred from its fields, a list of lists, a list of a `Drop` type freed with it, a generic function returning a borrow, and a generic type with a `Drop` method of its own, run per instance |
| net.snello | Sockets: a server task on a port the system picks, a client over the loopback, `bufio` over a connection, the end of a connection, a refused dial worded as Go words it and of `Kind` `Refused`, the Errors of a port out of range and of a name with no address, a dial with no host, a read into a buffer with no room, a listener and a dial on IPv6 and the addresses they print, a name listened on and dialed with its addresses tried in turn, an IPv4 client of a listener on every address of both families |
| traits.snello | Traits as bounds, default methods and trait fields: a trait with required methods and a default, a trait refining it, a trait with a field read by its default and set in literals, a type inheriting the default, one overriding it with `super` and one taking a refining trait's version that wraps the original with `super`, a `mut` method calling a `ref` default through `super`, a `super` that reaches a definition placed between a trait and the one it refines, a `[]Shape` holding three types and dispatching to each, a generic function taking that slice through its bound, a trait field written through a trait value, a `mut` method and a consuming method through a trait value, a boxed `Drop` type dropped with its trait value, a trait value returned from a function and called on or lent at once, one passed by value, an inherited method and a trait field reached through a refining trait's value, a boxed generic instance, a struct holding a trait value whose method takes the struct, a `mut` method on a slice element of trait values, `==` through a written `Eq`, a map key through a written `Hash` and `Eq`, and a derived `Eq` and `Hash` used by `==`, by name and as a map key, a generic type whose methods call its bounded parameter's and whose instances get their own copy of the default, generic functions bounded by the traits with each call going to the type argument's own method, a bound met by a nested instance, and a `Drop` method checked against the standard trait |
| standard.snello | The standard traits: `+`, `-`, `*`, unary `-` on a struct through its `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul<f64>` and `Neg` methods, an operator on a type that owns memory consuming both operands and dropping them inside, a generic sum bounded by `Add` over `[]int` and over the struct, a generic scale bounded by `Mul<f64>` over the struct and over `f64`, an operator on a value reached through a `mut` borrow, compound assignment on a variable and on a slice element, a literal right operand taking the method's parameter type, `Cmp`, `Clone` and `Hash` derived from the fields of a struct and of an enum with payloads, a derived `Clone` of a struct holding a slice, `Cmp` on numbers and strings, an `Ordering` printed and matched on, a map keyed by a derived `Hash`, and a largest-of bounded by `Ord` and `Clone` over numbers, a struct and an enum |
| library.snello | The standard library written in Snello: the `math` package imported, its constant read, its functions called and one the runtime provides, a library function passed as a value, a float printed with a precision, and a top-level constant of the program's own |
| text.snello | The `strings` and `strconv` packages written in Snello: a `Builder` written to, read and reset, `Repeat` and `Join`, `ToLower` and `ToUpper`, `Fields` through the package, `Atoi` with each of its errors, `Itoa`, `ParseFloat` and `FormatFloat`, an `Error`'s fields read, the conversions between a string and its bytes, `fmt.Fprintln` and `Fprintf` writing to `os.Stdout`, and widths in a format |
| order.snello | The `sort` and `time` packages written in Snello: `Sort` on numbers, strings and a struct whose `Ord` is derived, `SortBy` with an order of the program's own, `Search` and `IsSorted`; a `Duration` written as a product of a constant, its arithmetic and its readings, a `Time` built, moved and compared, and `Sleep` measured with `Since` |
| arena.snello | The `arena` package written in Snello: an `Arena` of strings inserted into, read, changed through `GetMut` and removed from; a stale `Index` answering `None` to `Get`, `GetMut` and `Remove` after its slot is reused while the new `Index` of the slot answers the new value; an `Index` printed as its slot and generation, and one slot reused through a thousand removals; the zero `Index` naming nothing; indices compared; every value removed and the free slots filled again; a tree of nodes linked by indices built through `GetMut` and walked from its root, and a removed subtree leaving its parent's link stale; an `Arena` dropped with values in it |
| shared.snello | The `rc` package written in Snello: an `Rc` of a string cloned, read through every handle, changed through `GetMut` only while it is the one handle, and counted; a value with a `Drop` method dropped when its last `Rc` goes and not before, a `Weak` that does not keep it alive, upgraded while the value is there and answering `None` after; a struct holding an `Rc` dropped with it; handles kept in a slice and popped; an `Rc` of an `Rc`; a `Weak` cloned; a `Weak` dropped while its `Rc` lives and `GetMut` once the `Weak` is gone; a link that may point at nothing as an optional `Weak`, since a handle has no zero value |
| buffered.snello | The `bufio` package written in Snello: a `Writer` over stdout holding what is written until its buffer fills or `Flush`, written to by its own methods and through `fmt.Fprintln` and `Fprintf`, and one with a two-byte buffer; a file written through a `Writer`, scanned line by line with the last line unterminated and the scanner empty after its last `Scan`, and read through a `Reader` by bytes, up to a delimiter, into a slice and to the end; a file copied through a `Reader` into a `Writer` with `io.Copy`; line endings with a carriage return and an empty line; a `Scanner` over an empty file and over a line longer than a block; and a writer that takes nothing, reported as a short write |
| iterators.snello | Generic traits: an `Iterator<T>` trait with a required `Next` and default adapters, one with a type parameter of its own, a `Range` implementing `Iterator<int>`, generic `MapIter` and `FilterIter` structs bounded by the trait and implementing it over their own parameters, a chain of `Map`, `Filter` and `Collect` over a named function and over closures, a generic method called on a call's result, and a `mut` method called on a temporary |
| arrays.snello | Arrays in the backend: an array of strings written to, printed, cloned inside a struct and dropped with every element released; an array of arrays; an array literal with the rest zero; an array copied whole and changed apart; a struct holding an array compared through its own `Eq` |
| drops.snello | Where values die: `Drop` methods printing in the order the compiler releases values, at scope ends, before returns, breaks and continues, in match arms, and for temporaries; a failed guard, conditional moves, a duplicate map key, a consumed closure capture, a deferred moved argument, a `take` through a borrow a call returned with the call run once, and a borrow of a temporary dropped with its statement |
| tasks.snello | Tasks and channels: a function, a library function, a generic instance, a method and a closure spawned, with a Copy capture copied and an owned one moved; each task cloning the channel handles it uses, and functions borrowing one through `ref chan<- T` and `ref <-chan T`; unbuffered and buffered channels, `close`, `for range ch`, `len` and `cap`; a `Drop` value crossing a channel and dropped by its receiver; every task ending before `main` returns |
| select.snello | `select` over receives and sends, with and without `default`: a case chosen at random among two ready channels, a send ready only while a receiver waits, a bare receive dropping its value, and a closed channel's `None` |
| sync.snello | The `sync` package: a counter shared by four tasks through `Arc<Mutex<int>>` with a `WaitGroup`, a map filled by three tasks through `Arc<RwLock<map[string]int>>` and summed under the read lock, a `Once` asked by three tasks, a `Drop` value dropped once by the last `Arc` handle, a hundred locks made and dropped in turn and a hundred held at once, and a `time.After` deadline in a `select` |
| unicode.snello | Text beyond ASCII: `ToUpper` and `ToLower` by Unicode's full case mapping, `ß` to `SS` and `İ` to `i` with a combining dot, a byte that is not UTF-8 read as U+FFFD, `Fields` and `Trim` on Unicode white space, `Split` with an empty separator by UTF-8 sequence and on an empty string, `Repeat`, `Join` and a `Builder`, `Contains` on a long text, and `Sort` on a struct through its `Cmp`|
| clocks.snello | Time arithmetic as Go's: a `Time` in 2286 round-tripping through `Unix`, comparisons across centuries, `Sub` saturating at the longest `Duration` either way, `Unix` rounding down and carrying nanoseconds into seconds, two `Now`s compared and subtracted on the monotonic clock, an `After` handing over a whole `Time` the runtime's timer made, `Duration.String` over every branch of Go's algorithm with `Round`, `Truncate` and `Abs` from Go's tests, a `Time` printed in UTC as Go prints one, across leap days, the first year and the year 9999, and a `Ticker` stopped or reset after a tick no one received, which leaves nothing in its channel |
| formats.snello | Printing as Go prints: floats in the shortest form with Go's exponent rule, `+Inf`, `-Inf` and `NaN`, an `f32` at its own precision, a precision on `%v`, `%s`, `%q` and `%d`, `%q` escaped as `strconv.Quote` escapes and an integer quoted as its rune, a `fmt.Stringer` printed as its `String` alone and inside a struct, `math.Abs`, `Min` and `Max` and the predeclared `min` and `max` on `-0` and `NaN`, `ParseFloat`'s grammar and the `Kind` of its error, and an `Rc`, a `Weak` and an `Arena` printed as what they hold |
| runes.snello | Text whole, the program chapter 19 is cut from: a range over a string giving each rune and its byte offset, `s.Runes()` and `string(rs)`, the counted loop over bytes, a string that is not valid UTF-8, the `unicode` package's classes, derived properties, categories, scripts and values, full case mapping and title case by words, `EqualIgnoreCase`, `unicode/utf8`, `unicode/utf16` as units and bytes, the normalization forms, and graphemes, words and sentences |
| zero.snello | No empty values, the program chapter 18 is cut from: the zero values of the types that have one, an optional where a value may be missing, a value built where it is declared when it depends on a condition, an optional `rc.Weak`, `replace` on a field of a type with no zero value and on an optional pointer, a map of such values read with `Get`, `strings.Repeat`'s option and a `WaitGroup` that will not count below zero |
| errors.snello | The `Error` trait: a message derived from the value for an enum, a struct and a type over `int`, `Source` giving a clone of the cause, the chain under `%+v` on the type and on a trait value of `Error`, `?` passing an `io.Error` and a `strconv.Error` into the variant holding each and into an `Error` value, and a trait value of `Error` or `fmt.Stringer` printed as its message |
| failures.snello | `bufio` when the file under it fails part way: a `Writer` keeping its first error for every later call and never writing a byte twice, a `Reader` keeping what it had read before a failure for the next `ReadString`, a `Scanner` giving the partial last line before `Err` |
| streams.snello | The edges of `io`, `bufio` and `os`: an `io.NewError` and the three ways an `Error` prints, with a path, without one, and with no `Op`; `ReadToString` naming the step that failed, on a directory and on an empty path; `WriteString` and `Remove` of a file, of a missing one and of a full directory; `MkdirTemp` putting its number where the pattern's last `*` is, and refusing a pattern with a `/`; `io.Copy` refusing a writer that claims more than it was given; a `Scanner` refusing a line past the limit `Buffer` set, over a reader that gives a few bytes a call and over a file; a `Reader` asked again after the end of the input, as a file being appended to is; and a `Writer` keeping its first error for an empty write too, with a size of zero taken as the default |
| alloc.snello | The allocator across tasks: strings of every size class and larger made by four tasks at once and released by `main` on another thread, each checked byte by byte on arrival and every tenth kept and checked again at the end, so a block handed out twice would show |
| iterate.snello | A range over any value with `Next`: one variable or a pair, an iterator lent or consumed, a map type with `Next` ranged as an iterator, a map's `Entry` from any place, below 0 and past the end |
| borrow-index.snello | An element reached by an index that calls, or of a call's result, matched, bound, lent and taken in place, the index computed once |
| deque.snello | The deque's buffer of untagged slots: elements that own memory pushed at both ends, wrapped, grown, changed in place, cleared and dropped with the deque, every block counted in a debug build |
| empty-array.snello | A zero-length array: its literal, its zero value and a field of one in a generic struct with a `Drop` |
| self-handles.snello | Types holding handles on themselves: a tree with `Weak` parents and `Rc` children, an `Arc` list, a node with a `Deque` of nodes, a `Weak` on a cell whose value is gone |

A program that reads files would have them in a folder named after it with the suffix `.files`, which the test copies beside the binary.
